key_insight: A small set of attention heads helps determine whether a multimodal AI follows visual or textual evidence when they disagree. These “arbitration heads” causally influence that choice, offering a target for controlling it at inference time.
problem_solved: Multimodal models can favor text or images even when that modality is less reliable for the task, producing unreliable answers when the inputs conflict.
method: Study how models choose between conflicting visual and textual evidence.
Identify attention heads that causally influence which modality drives the prediction.
Use these arbitration heads as a basis for lightweight inference-time control; the provided abstract is truncated before the full method is described.
impact: This work points toward more controllable multimodal systems that can be guided toward task-appropriate evidence rather than default modality preferences. The provided excerpt does not include quantitative results or implementation details.

paper_title: Beyond Modality Preference: Controlling Multimodal Arbitration under Modality Conflict in MLLMs
paper_authors: Zhaoying Pan, Shenyu Lu, Jun Hui Wong, Junyi Chai, Xiaoqian Wang
